_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Georgia covering Colchis and Iberia (ancient kingdoms), Christianisation (AD 337), Golden Age under Tamar the Great, Mongol/Timurid invasions, Persian/Ottoman partition, Russian annexation (1801), Georgian Democratic Republic 1918, Soviet Georgia, Stalin (born Gori), Abkhazia and South Ossetia conflicts, Rose Revolution 2003, 2008 Russia-Georgia War, EU candidacy, and democratic development.

religion.note: Georgian Orthodox Church is autocephalous; one of oldest Christian churches (AD 337, second after Armenia)

ethnic_groups.name: Georgian
ethnic_groups.notes: South Caucasian (Kartvelian) language family; unique alphabet (Mkhedruli, 33 letters); sub-groups include Megrelian, Svan, Laz (mostly in Türkiye); wine culture (8,000 years, qvevri)

ethnic_groups.name: Azerbaijani
ethnic_groups.notes: Kvemo Kartli and Kakheti; Turkic; Shia Muslim; largest minority; some cultural tensions

ethnic_groups.name: Armenian
ethnic_groups.notes: Samtskhe-Javakheti (Javakheti); Armenian Apostolic; historically significant in Tbilisi

ethnic_groups.name: Russian
ethnic_groups.notes: Urban; declining since independence; Molokans, Doukhobors (spiritual Christian sects)

ethnic_groups.name: Ossetian
ethnic_groups.notes: Iranian (Indo-European); South Ossetia (de facto independent/Russian-controlled since 2008); most displaced

ethnic_groups.name: Abkhaz
ethnic_groups.notes: Northwest Caucasian; Abkhazia (de facto independent/Russian-controlled since 1993); ~250,000 IDPs in Georgia proper

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Kist/Chechen, Greek, Kurdish, Assyrian)
ethnic_groups.notes: Kist (Chechen) in Pankisi Gorge; Pontic Greeks (declining); Kurdish Yezidi; small Assyrian community

geography.terrain: Mountainous; Greater Caucasus in north, Lesser Caucasus in south; Kolkheti lowlands west; fertile Kakheti valley east
geography.notes: Crossroads of Europe and Asia; Greater Caucasus provides natural border with Russia; Abkhazia and South Ossetia occupied by Russia (20% of territory); Black Sea coastline.

economy_extended.notes: Remarkably high ease of doing business rank; post-2022 boom from Russian immigration/capital flight; wine tourism; transit corridor (BTC pipeline, BTK railway); EU candidate status 2023.

health.notes: Universal Healthcare Programme (UHC) since 2013; high physician density but quality uneven; medical tourism growing (dental, cosmetic); Soviet-era facilities being modernized.

food_agriculture.notes: 8,000-year winemaking tradition (qvevri method, UNESCO heritage); world's oldest wine culture; hazelnut top export crop; tea production in western Georgia; organic farming growing.

energy.notes: Hydropower 80% of electricity; BTC oil pipeline transit country; Shah Deniz gas (Azerbaijan to Europe) transits Georgia; energy dependency on imports; wind/solar potential underexploited; Namakhvani HPP project cancelled after protests.

transport.notes: BTK railway (Baku-Tbilisi-Kars) links Caucasus and Turkey; Poti/Batumi Black Sea ports; Middle Corridor transit route (China-Europe); Tbilisi International Airport; mountainous terrain limits infrastructure.

tourism.notes: Tourism boom post-2010; wine tourism major draw; ski resorts (Gudauri, Bakuriani); UNESCO 8,000-year qvevri winemaking; culinary tourism; e-visa/visa-free for many; Digital Nomad visa programme.

legal_system.notes: EU candidate country (Dec 2023); constitutional reforms ongoing; judiciary independence concerns; Rose Revolution (2003) led to governance reforms; foreign agent law controversy (2024, EU accession implications).

human_rights_gender.notes: Democratic backsliding concerns (foreign agent law 2024); anti-LGBTQ+ violence (2021 Tbilisi Pride attacks); patriarchal traditions in rural areas; EU conditionality on human rights reforms; media polarized.

security_stability.notes: 20% of territory occupied by Russia (Abkhazia, South Ossetia since 2008 war); 'borderization' creeping annexation; NATO aspirations blocked by Russia; 280,000+ IDPs from 1990s/2008 conflicts.

unesco_intangible_heritage: Living culture of three writing systems of Georgian alphabet
cultural_heritage.notes: One of the world's oldest and most unique alphabets (14 letters, 3 scripts); 8,000-year wine tradition (world's oldest); Georgian polyphonic singing sent into space on Voyager Golden Record.

comparative_rankings.notes: Exceptionally high ease of doing business; strong anti-corruption progress post-Rose Revolution; occupied territories drag security scores; EU candidacy milestone.
comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Irakli Kobakhidze
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: Georgian Dream party; Bidzina Ivanishvili (oligarch) is de facto power; 2024 elections disputed; anti-EU/pro-Russia pivot; Foreign Agent Law 2024 sparked protests

president.name: Salome Zourabichvili
president.title: President (ceremonial)
president.notes: French-born Georgian; independent; increasingly at odds with Georgian Dream; pro-EU; term expires 2024

former_leaders.name: Zviad Gamsakhurdia
former_leaders.notes: First president; nationalist; overthrown in civil war; died 1993

former_leaders.name: Eduard Shevardnadze
former_leaders.notes: Former Soviet foreign minister under Gorbachev; stabilised Georgia; corruption; ousted by Rose Revolution

former_leaders.name: Mikheil Saakashvili
former_leaders.notes: Rose Revolution; UNM; Western-oriented; economic reforms; 2008 war with Russia; lost South Ossetia; later jailed in absentia; convicted after return 2021

former_leaders.name: Giorgi Margvelashvili
former_leaders.notes: Georgian Dream; fell out with Ivanishvili

910.name: Colchis and Iberia — Ancient Georgian Kingdoms
910.description: The ancient kingdoms of Colchis (western Georgia) and Iberia (eastern Georgia), their connections to the Greek world through the Argonaut legend, and the pre-Roman Kartvelian civilization.

sub_clusters.name: Kingdom of Colchis
sub_clusters.description: Colchis on the Black Sea coast, famed in Greek mythology as the destination of Jason and the Argonauts, its gold-panning traditions, Greek colonial settlements at Phasis and Dioscurias.
key_events: Colchis enters Greek mythology as the land of the Golden Fleece and Medea
Greek colonies established at Phasis and Dioscurias along the Colchian coast (6th century BC)

sub_clusters.name: Kingdom of Iberia (Kartli)
sub_clusters.description: The founding of the Kingdom of Iberia (Kartli) under King Pharnavaz I, the creation of the Georgian script, and interactions with the Seleucid and later Parthian empires.

910.name: Roman-Iranian Contested Georgia
910.description: Georgia caught between Rome and the Parthian/Sassanid empires, the Roman campaigns of Pompey and later emperors, and the strategic importance of the Caucasian passes.

sub_clusters.name: Roman Expansion into the Caucasus
sub_clusters.description: Pompey's campaigns in the Caucasus, the Roman client-state relationship with Iberia, and the strategic importance of controlling the Dariali and Derbent passes against nomadic incursions.

sub_clusters.name: Iberian Kings and Dual Suzerainty
sub_clusters.description: The Iberian kingdom navigating between Roman and Parthian/Sassanid overlords, the Christianization of Iberia by St. Nino, and the establishment of Christianity as the state religion.

920.name: Christianization and Early Medieval Georgia
920.description: The adoption of Christianity, the development of the Georgian alphabet, the rise of the Bagrationi dynasty, Arab emirate rule in Tbilisi, and the unification of the Georgian polities.

sub_clusters.name: Christianization of Georgia
sub_clusters.description: St. Nino's conversion of King Mirian III of Iberia, adoption of Christianity as the state religion around 337 AD, the development of the unique Georgian alphabet, and the flourishing of Georgian ecclesiastical literature.
key_events: King Mirian III adopts Christianity as state religion of Iberia (c. 337 AD)
Creation of the Georgian alphabet attributed to King Pharnavaz I or Mesrop Mashtots' circle

sub_clusters.name: Arab Emirate of Tbilisi
sub_clusters.description: The Arab conquest and establishment of the Emirate of Tbilisi, the coexistence of Muslim and Christian populations, and the gradual Georgian reassertion leading to David the Builder.

sub_clusters.name: Bagrationi Unification
sub_clusters.description: The Bagrationi dynasty's gradual unification of the fragmented Georgian principalities, culminating in Bagrat III's creation of a united Kingdom of Georgia.

920.name: Golden Age of Georgia
920.description: The zenith of medieval Georgia under David the Builder and Queen Tamar, the expansion of Georgian power across the Caucasus, and the golden age of Georgian literature and architecture.

sub_clusters.name: David the Builder
sub_clusters.description: King David IV 'the Builder' who liberated Tbilisi, defeated the Seljuks at the Battle of Didgori, reformed the military and church, and laid the foundations of Georgia's golden age.
key_events: Battle of Didgori — decisive Georgian victory over the Seljuks (1121)
David the Builder liberates Tbilisi from the Arab emirate (1122)

sub_clusters.name: Queen Tamar and Cultural Zenith
sub_clusters.description: Queen Tamar's reign as the height of Georgian political and cultural power, Shota Rustaveli's epic poem 'The Knight in the Panther's Skin,' military expansion, and support for the Trebizond Empire.
key_events: Shota Rustaveli composes 'The Knight in the Panther's Skin' (c. 1196)
Georgian armies help establish the Empire of Trebizond (1204)

sub_clusters.name: Georgian Architectural Golden Age
sub_clusters.description: The construction of masterpieces such as Gelati Monastery, Bagrati Cathedral, and the cave city of Vardzia, representing the pinnacle of Georgian medieval architecture.

930.name: Mongol and Timurid Devastation
930.description: The Mongol invasion ending Georgia's golden age, the fragmentation of the kingdom, Timurid invasions, and the disintegration into rival kingdoms and principalities.

sub_clusters.name: Mongol Conquest and Ilkhanate Period
sub_clusters.description: The devastating Mongol invasions, Georgia's incorporation into the Ilkhanate, heavy tribute, population loss, and the brief Georgian alliance with Mongol Christians.

sub_clusters.name: Timurid Invasions and Fragmentation
sub_clusters.description: Timur's eight devastating campaigns through Georgia, the destruction of cities and churches, and the final breakup of the Georgian kingdom into Kartli, Kakheti, and Imereti.

930.name: Ottoman-Safavid Contested Georgia
930.description: The fragmented Georgian kingdoms caught between the Ottoman and Safavid empires, forced conversions, the heroic resistance of Georgian kings, and the devastating raids.

sub_clusters.name: Safavid Domination of Eastern Georgia
sub_clusters.description: Kartli and Kakheti under Safavid suzerainty, forced conversions to Islam, Shah Abbas I's devastating 1616 punitive campaign, and the Georgian nobility's struggle to preserve identity.
key_events: Shah Abbas I devastates Kakheti and deports 100,000 Georgians (1614–1617)
The Bakhtrioni uprising — Georgians revolt against Safavid rule (1659)

sub_clusters.name: Ottoman Domination of Western Georgia
sub_clusters.description: Imereti and the western Georgian principalities under Ottoman influence, the spread of Islam in Adjara and Lazistan, and the fragmentation of western Georgian political authority.

940.name: Russian Annexation and Imperial Georgia
940.description: The Treaty of Georgievsk with Russia, the subsequent annexation of the Georgian kingdoms, the abolition of the Georgian church's autocephaly, and the growth of Georgian nationalism.

sub_clusters.name: Treaty of Georgievsk and Annexation
sub_clusters.description: King Heraclius II's protection treaty with Russia, the Persian sack of Tbilisi in 1795, Russia's unilateral abolition of the Kartli-Kakheti kingdom, and the absorption of all Georgian territories.
key_events: Treaty of Georgievsk places eastern Georgia under Russian protection (1783)
Aga Mohammad Khan of Persia sacks Tbilisi (1795)
Russia abolishes the Georgian monarchy and directly annexes Kartli-Kakheti (1801)

sub_clusters.name: Russian Imperial Period and Nationalism
sub_clusters.description: Russian colonial administration, the abolition of the Georgian church's autocephaly, the development of Georgian romantic nationalism by Ilia Chavchavadze, and the Bolshevik movement in Georgia.

950.name: Democratic Republic and Sovietization of Georgia
950.description: The Georgian Democratic Republic as an independent social-democratic state, its international recognition, and the Red Army invasion that ended Georgian independence.

sub_clusters.name: Georgian Democratic Republic
sub_clusters.description: The establishment of the Georgian Democratic Republic under Menshevik leadership, women's suffrage, progressive social policies, and recognition by major powers.
key_events: Georgian Democratic Republic proclaimed in Tbilisi (May 26, 1918)
Red Army invades Georgia, ending independence (February 1921)

sub_clusters.name: August 1924 Uprising
sub_clusters.description: The failed anti-Soviet uprising across Georgia in August 1924, brutal Bolshevik repression, and the consolidation of Soviet power.

950.name: Soviet Georgia
950.description: Georgia as a Soviet republic, Stalin's Georgian origins, industrialization, the 1956 Tbilisi protests, the national movement, and the April 9 tragedy.

sub_clusters.name: Stalinist Era and Georgia's Son
sub_clusters.description: Georgia under Soviet rule with its native son Joseph Stalin (Ioseb Jughashvili) as supreme leader, forced collectivization, purges of Georgian intelligentsia, and WWII mobilization.

sub_clusters.name: 1956 Protests and Post-Stalin Era
sub_clusters.description: The 1956 Tbilisi demonstrations against de-Stalinization, the shadow economy, the 1978 language protests preserving Georgian's constitutional status, and Eduard Shevardnadze's rise.
key_events: Mass protests in Tbilisi against Khrushchev's de-Stalinization; Soviet troops fire on crowds (1956)
Mass protests successfully defend Georgian language's constitutional status (1978)

sub_clusters.name: April 9 Tragedy and Independence
sub_clusters.description: The April 9, 1989 Soviet massacre of peaceful protesters in Tbilisi, the rise of Zviad Gamsakhurdia, and the declaration of Georgian independence.
key_events: Soviet troops kill 21 peaceful protesters in Tbilisi with poison gas and shovels (April 9, 1989)
Georgia declares independence from the Soviet Union (April 9, 1991)

960.name: Independent Georgia and Western Orientation
960.description: Post-Soviet Georgia's civil wars, the Rose Revolution, the 2008 Russia-Georgia war, EU and NATO aspirations, and the contested political direction of the country.

sub_clusters.name: Civil Wars and Shevardnadze Era
sub_clusters.description: The Gamsakhurdia coup, civil war, separatist conflicts in South Ossetia and Abkhazia, Russian-backed ethnic cleansing of Georgians, and Shevardnadze's corrupt governance.

sub_clusters.name: Rose Revolution and Saakashvili Reforms
sub_clusters.description: The peaceful Rose Revolution deposing Shevardnadze, Mikheil Saakashvili's sweeping anti-corruption reforms, military modernization, and the pivot toward NATO and EU.
key_events: Rose Revolution — peaceful overthrow of Shevardnadze government (November 2003)
Russia-Georgia War over South Ossetia; Russia recognizes breakaway territories (August 2008)

sub_clusters.name: Democratic Backsliding and EU Path
sub_clusters.description: Georgian Dream's rise to power, EU candidacy granted in 2023, the controversial foreign agents law, mass protests, and the ongoing tension between Euro-Atlantic integration and Russian influence.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
